issues.failure_explanation: The proof never shows that $\Linop{C}$ maps $\mathbb{M}$ into $\mathbb{L}$; membership in $\Kernel{c}{\Batrix{A}\Matrix{B}}$ follows from $\Batrix{A}\Matrix{BC}x=0$, but orthogonality to $\Kernel{}{\Matrix{B}}$ does not. In the usual-matrix specialization $A=[0,1]$, $B=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $C=[[1,0],[1,0]]$, one has $\mathbb{M}=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}$ and $\mathbb{L}=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}$, yet $Ce_1=(1,1)^\trans\notin\mathbb{L}$, so the asserted injective operator $\mathbb{M}\to\mathbb{L}$ does not exist. The inequality itself remains true by applying rank-nullity to $T=\Batrix{A}|_{\Image{c}{\Matrix{B}}}$ and $R=\Matrix{B}|_{\Image{}{\Matrix{C}}}$.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the kernel argument with the standard restriction argument: for $T=\Batrix{A}|_{\Image{c}{\Matrix{B}}}$ and $R=\Matrix{B}|_{\Image{}{\Matrix{C}}}$, rank-nullity on $T|_{\Image{}{R}}$ gives $\Rank{c}{\Batrix{A}\Matrix{BC}} \ge \Rank{c}{\Batrix{A}\Matrix{B}} + \rank{\Matrix{BC}} - \rank{\Matrix{B}}$.
issues.overall_effect: The printed proof of the Frobenius inequality is unsupported as written; the later Sylvester step in Lemma~\ref{lemma:rank_properties} inherits the gap, although the statements survive after the restriction argument is restored.
issues.title: Frobenius-inequality proof uses a restriction that need not land in the claimed subspace
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement is true and a standard replacement argument exists, but the printed proof contains a false operator construction and a downstream Sylvester use is repaired only by supplying that argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for norms $\Norm{\cdot}{\circ}$ on $\F^{n}$ and $\Norm{\cdot}{\bullet}$ on $\Hilb^{m}$, the $\circ \to \bullet$ operator norm

issues.failure_explanation: As written, the left side multiplies a Bochner isometry $\Batrix{Q}$ by a Bochner matrix $\Batrix{A}$, while the right side is a norm of a usual matrix $\Matrix{A}$; the objects and dimensions do not match. The proofs consistently use the corrected meaning: for a Bochner $\Batrix{Q}$ with orthonormal columns and a usual matrix $\Matrix{C}$, one should require $\Norm{\Batrix{Q}\Matrix{C}}{\bullet}=\Norm{\Matrix{C}}{\circ}$. Under the literal definition with $\Hilb=\F$, taking $\Batrix{Q}=\Matrix{I}$ would force every associated usual norm to be the Frobenius norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the clause as left-invariance on usual matrices: for every Bochner $\Batrix{Q}$ with orthonormal columns and every compatible usual matrix $\Matrix{C}$, require $\Norm{\Batrix{Q}\Matrix{C}}{\bullet}=\Norm{\Matrix{C}}{\circ}$, with the associated usual norm unitarily invariant.
issues.overall_effect: Every statement quantifying over “unitarily invariant” Bochner norms, and the results proved through that notion, are formally not well-founded until the clause is repaired; the intended proofs already use the repaired left-invariance property.
issues.title: Definition of a unitarily invariant Bochner norm is type-inconsistent
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local clarification of a definition and all subsequent proofs already use the clarified meaning, so no rate, guarantee, or proof architecture is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.

issues.failure_explanation: Full column/row rank of the outer usual factors is not sufficient. Already for $\Hilb=\F$, take $B=[[1,0],[0,1],[1,1]]$, $A=[[1,0],[0,0]]$, $C=I_2$. Then $B$ has full column rank and $C$ has full row rank, but $(BAC)^\pinv=[[1/2,0,1/2],[0,0,0]]$, whereas $C^\pinv A^\pinv B^\pinv = A B^\pinv = [[2/3,-1/3,1/3],[0,0,0]]$. The displayed substitution only checks the uses of $B^\pinv B=I$ and $CC^\pinv=I$; it does not verify the self-adjoint Moore-Penrose conditions, which fail here.

failure_location.quote: If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypotheses to isometries, e.g. require $B^*B=I_m$ and $CC^*=I_n$ (orthonormal columns/rows), or add the corresponding commutativity/compatibility hypotheses under which the Penrose product law holds.
issues.overall_effect: This pseudoinverse identity is false in the stated generality, even for ordinary matrices viewed as Bochner matrices over $\F$; later text does not appear to rely on this exact general identity, but the lemma overstates a basic property.
issues.title: General full-rank pseudoinverse product rule is false
issues.why_classification: A correct product rule survives only after a genuine hypothesis strengthening or extra compatibility condition; the general full-rank promise as stated must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By definition, an SVD of a Bochner matrix corresponds to a compact SVD of a usual matrix and is not defined when the Bochner matrix is identically zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Bochner SVDs only for non-zero matrices, but Theorem~\ref{theorem:bochner_hosvd} is stated for every $\Batrix{A}\in\Hilb^{m\times n}$ and immediately invokes two SVDs. At $\Batrix{A}=0$ the objects in the statement are undefined as defined in the paper; the desired conclusion is trivial there.

failure_location.quote: For $\Batrix{A} \in \Hilb^{m \times n}$, let $\Batrix{A} = \Batrix{U} \Matrix{\Sigma} \Matrix{V}^*$ and $\Batrix{A}^\trans = \Batrix{P} \Matrix{\Lambda} \Matrix{Q}^*$ be SVDs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\Batrix{A}$ is non-zero, or explicitly adopt the empty-SVD convention for the zero matrix.
issues.overall_effect: Only the degenerate zero case is ill-posed; the quasioptimality bound for non-zero Bochner matrices is unchanged.
issues.title: HOSVD theorem omits the non-zero hypothesis needed for its SVDs
issues.why_classification: This is a standard boundary hypothesis; adding it preserves the entire statement and proof for the intended non-zero regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $n_{\mathrm{rook}} = 0$, the rows are selected at random and the choice of columns is adaptive.

issues.failure_explanation: If $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$, the loop body is never executed, so $i_*$ is never assigned although it is returned. The same defect is present in $\scup{rook}(\Batrix{A},j_0,n_{\mathrm{rook}})$. The paper explicitly uses $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$ as the random-row/adaptive-column regime, so this is not a harmless convention: the written procedure cannot produce the intended output.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Initialize the row index before the loop or pass the candidate row into the zero-round case, so that $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$ returns the starting candidate $(i_s,j_s)$ unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Both rook procedures and their ACA/ABCD callers are not well-defined at the advertised boundary $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$; the numerical comparison involving $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$ presupposes the unwritten intended behavior.
issues.title: Rook pivoting is undefined for zero rounds
issues.why_classification: A one-line initialization/contract fix restores the intended $n_{\mathrm{rook}}=0$ behavior and leaves all algorithmic guarantees and reported experiments intact.

issues.failure_explanation: For $-u''-\alpha^2u=\cos(\beta x)$, the sine coefficients satisfy $(k^2-\alpha^2)u_k = \frac{2}{\pi}\, k[1-(-1)^k\cos(\beta\pi)]/(k^2-\beta^2)$, so the denominator should be $k^2-\alpha^2$, not $k^2+\alpha^2$. As written, the displayed Fourier series solves $-u''+\alpha^2u=\cos(\beta x)$. Moreover, the written operator $-d^2-\alpha^2$ on $[0,\pi]$ is resonant at $\alpha=1,2$, which lie inside the advertised parameter box $[0,2]\times[0,2]$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the displayed BVP to $-u''+\alpha^2u=\cos(\beta x)$ so it matches the Fourier solution and the computed errors; changing the denominator to $k^2-\alpha^2$ instead would force removal or special treatment of the resonant parameters $\alpha=1,2$ in the advertised box.
issues.overall_effect: The linear BVP experiment, Figure~\ref{fig:ode_bvp}, and the prose conclusions drawn from it are tied to an inconsistent model statement; the general Bochner theory and the separate FEniCS Stokes experiment are not affected.
issues.title: Displayed ODE model and its Fourier solution have inconsistent signs
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, but there is a genuine choice of mathematical repairs and the written operator is indefinite/resonant on the advertised parameter regime, so it withdraws or alters the displayed model rather than being a mere forced typo.
